key_insight: O²LaF uses one pretrained video Diffusion Transformer (DiT) as the starting point for two tasks: inferring hidden actions from visual changes and predicting how those actions change the scene.
problem_solved: Videos show what changes but rarely label the actions responsible. Existing latent action learning approaches often learn the dynamics largely from scratch rather than leveraging a pretrained video generator.
method: Initialize both inverse and forward dynamics models from the same pretrained video DiT.
Use inverse dynamics to infer latent actions from visual transitions.
Use forward dynamics to model visual changes conditioned on latent actions. The supplied abstract is truncated, so further adaptation details are unavailable.
impact: This approach could let practitioners reuse pretrained video-generation knowledge for self-supervised action learning, reducing reliance on explicit action labels. The supplied excerpt does not report quantitative results.
visual_elements: A shared pretrained video DiT branching into inverse and forward dynamics models.
Inverse dynamics diagram: before-and-after frames → inferred latent action.
Forward dynamics diagram: current frame + latent action → predicted visual change.
A short video strip highlighting visible motion alongside an unlabeled action icon.
paper_title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
paper_authors: Yuxin Jiang, Wenqiang Sun, Jiaqi Li, Yuchao Gu, Lvmin Zhang
